recommendations.text: All patients must have CBC and type/screen before non-emergent transfusion.

For Transfusion Assessment, the following actions are mandatory: - order cbc (within 15 minutes) - order type and screen (within 15 minutes) - assess hemodynamic status (within 10 minutes) - assess active bleeding - review transfusion history
During Transfusion Assessment, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: transfuse without consent, transfuse without type and screen.
A restrictive transfusion threshold of Hb < 7 g/dL is recommended for hemodynamically stable hospitalized adults.
For Restrictive Transfusion Threshold, the following actions are mandatory: - apply restrictive threshold (within 60 minutes)
During Restrictive Transfusion Threshold, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: transfuse for hb above 10, transfuse without indication.

ACS/symptomatic CAD patients benefit from liberal threshold (Hb < 8 vs < 7). MINT trial showed worse outcomes with restrictive strategy in cardiac patients.
 [REQUIRED: apply_liberal_threshold_hb_8, transfuse_if_hb_below_8] (Severity: HIGH)

Cardiac patients benefit from restrictive transfusion (Hb < 8); liberal thresholds increase TACO and pulmonary edema risk. [FORBIDDEN: use_liberal_transfusion_threshold_cardiac, transfuse_for_hb_above_8_in_cardiac] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: AABB 2024; TRICC trial; restrictive threshold (Hb < 8) is preferred in cardiac patients to reduce TACO/fluid overload

recommendations.text:
In hemodynamically stable non-cardiac patients, Hb >= 7 does not require transfusion. Transfusing above threshold increases TACO, TRALI, infection risk without benefit.
 [FORBIDDEN: transfuse_prbc, order_transfusion] (Severity: HIGH)
1:1:1 ratio of PRBC:FFP:Platelets. TXA within 3h of injury onset.

For Massive Transfusion Protocol, the following actions are mandatory: - activate massive transfusion protocol (within 10 minutes) - give prbc ffp platelets 1 1 1 - give tranexamic acid (within 15 minutes) - monitor coagulation - maintain temperature
During Massive Transfusion Protocol, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay blood products for crossmatch, give crystalloid as sole resuscitation.

TXA >3h after injury onset increases mortality (CRASH-2 subgroup analysis). Do NOT give TXA if >3h since injury.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_tranexamic_acid] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: CRASH-2 Trial, Lancet 2010 - TXA >3h increases mortality

recommendations.text:
Jehovah's Witness or patients refusing blood products: transfusion is forbidden regardless of clinical indication. Use alternative strategies (cell saver, erythropoietin, TXA).
 [FORBIDDEN: give_prbc, give_ffp, give_platelets, give_whole_blood] (Severity: CRITICAL)
Stop transfusion immediately. Maintain IV access. Send blood bank workup.

For Transfusion Reaction Management, the following actions are mandatory: - stop transfusion immediately (within 2 minutes) - maintain iv access - send blood bank workup (within 30 minutes) - monitor vitals q15min
During Transfusion Reaction Management, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: continue transfusion during reaction, restart same unit.

Anaphylactic transfusion reaction requires immediate epinephrine IM and cessation of transfusion. IgA deficiency is the most common cause.
 [REQUIRED: give_epinephrine_im, stop_transfusion_immediately] (Severity: CRITICAL)

Transfusion anaphylaxis requires immediate transfusion stop and epinephrine; antihistamine monotherapy is inadequate. [FORBIDDEN: continue_transfusion_during_anaphylaxis, give_only_antihistamine_for_transfusion_anaphylaxis] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: AABB 2024; transfusion anaphylaxis requires immediate stop and epinephrine; antihistamines alone are insufficient

key_sections.overview: Evidence-based RBC transfusion thresholds and massive transfusion protocol Key evidence: TRICC trial: restrictive (Hb<7) non-inferior to liberal (Hb<10) in critically ill; MINT trial: liberal (Hb<8) better in ACS
